title: Existence and minimal-coupling uniqueness of the Markov-quantile law for arbitrary real-line probability marginals
source_title: The Markov-quantile process attached to a family of marginals
author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
difficulty_reason: Kolmogorov extension does not itself supply transition kernels that are simultaneously Markov-consistent and minimal among increasing-kernel couplings. The authors construct the monotone supremum on quantile levels and prove convergence and compatibility using a contraction metric on fixed-marginal couplings. The separate product-coupling induction establishes minimality and uniqueness without introducing temporal regularity assumptions.
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 9 (2022), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.177

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. TheoremA(a) for an arbitrary family of Borel probability measures on the real line indexed by all real times. Canonical law on the cylindrical sigma-algebra, increasing transition kernels, minimal lower-orthant couplings and finite-product approximation retained; no strong Markov, continuous-path, martingale or Wasserstein-energy conclusion. Complete new stochastic-order supremum, quantile-level averaging, metric contraction, composition consistency and minimality induction read. Kolmogorov–Daniell extension, disintegration, Portmanteau and Lebesgue differentiation are explicit established foundations. Fixed marginals are essential in the authored uniform-CDF metric and closure proof. Separate convergence TheoremB and Kellerer generalization not counted as parameter variants. Minor indices in printed compositions are unambiguously fixed by adjacent explicit kernel formulas; no altered mathematical construction supplied.
